_README: Detector roster for the 2026-09 evaluation of the ORIGINAL benchmark
(the six generators already in the dataset). 22 detectors.
OpenAI tier ladder: gpt-5.6-sol ($4/$20) / terra ($2/$12) / luna ($0.20/$1.20); GPT-6: astra / sol ($2/$10) / luna ($0.10/$0.50).
Thinking knobs follow the convention detect.py records for the published runs:
extra_body and gemini_thinking_level are NEVER set. Each model's per-entry note
records its documented default AND a measured token count, because the two did
not always agree — GPT-5.6 documents a 'medium' default yet spends only ~45
reasoning tokens here, while gemini-3.1-pro spends ~1175. `stream` is then set
to match: thinking-by-default DashScope models and the omni line (whose doc says
stream must be set to True) stream; the rest do not.
This is a MIXED condition, not a controlled one, and it is not even uniform
across vendors: Gemini cannot disable thinking at all, Grok rejects
reasoning_effort='none', and GPT-5.4-mini measures 0 reasoning tokens while
GPT-5.6 measures ~45. Any claim about reasoning needs its own ablation.
at its vendor default — the convention README.md states for the published
Image input is verified per model, not assumed: this deployment's DashScope
gateway silently drops the image for text-only models (deepseek-v4-pro
answered 'no image' while returning HTTP 200), so every entry is qualified by
check_models.py --vision-check, a two-image differential test.
Usage:
python tools/check_models.py --vision-check --models-config config/models_eval.json
python tools/detect.py --models-config config/models_eval.json ...
DashScope key slots balance LATENCY, not just rate limits: the three 60s+ models (qwen3.7-plus / -max / -flash) sit one per key.
